newsitem.title: JAPAN: Jump in Japan car exports rekindles trade fears.
newsitem.headline: Jump in Japan car exports rekindles trade fears.

text.p: Japanese vehicle exports to the United States jumped in February, according to industry figures released on Thursday, rekindling the prospects of another bitter trade row between the two superpowers.

Shipments to the United States rose nearly 10 percent in February to 98,434 units, marking the sixth straight gain on a year-on-year basis, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers' Association (JAMA) announced.
Overall vehicle exports rose 5.0 percent from a year earlier to 341,169 units, the ninth straight month they have gained on year-on-year basis, it said.

"I feel uneasy about rising exports. It will revive trade friction with the United States because recent Japanese exports are mainly based on shipments to the United States," Nomura Research analyst Seiji Sugiura said.
The situation will likely worsen, with further gains expected, analysts said.
"Japan's overall exports in 1997/98 are likely to go up by two percent to three percent from 1996/97, helped by the weak yen," Kankaku Research senior analyst Nobuaki Yanachi said.

Japanese carmakers are expected to continue boosting exports in the first half of the year as domestic sales slump after an April 1 increase in the domestic sales tax to five percent from the current three percent.
For carmakers, exports are more profitable than comparable domestic sales as long as the dollar stays above 100 yen, industry analysts say. It is currently trading around 124 yen.
The red flag is already up, analysts said.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said last Friday that Japan may be taking advantage of a healthy U.S. economy to export its way out of its economic woes.

The warning came at a time when Japan's trade surplus grew in February for the first time in over two years. The surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, grew 12.3 percent from a year ago.
Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato has already moved to ease U.S. jitters by asking automotive industry leaders to carefully moderate their exports.
A car industry leader meanwhile played down the worries.

JAMA chairman Yoshifumi Tsuji told reporters last week that Japan's vehicle exports in 1997/98 would remain flat or slightly lower than the year before, dampening worries about any sharp rally in exports.
